newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares close up despite Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares close up despite Deng's death.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed up on Thursday with market sentiment calming after opening sharply down on the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, brokers said.
The index was up 1.78 points or 1.26 percent to 143.53 points on volume of 42.2 million shares worth HK$214.7 million.
Shenzhen's domestic A share index fell 7.54 points or 2.11 percent to 350.59 points, rebounding from the opening level close to the 10 percent limit-down.
"Deng's death is without a doubt the most important market factor today," said one trader.
On the A share market, Sichuan Yinshan Chemical Industry (Group) Co Ltd performed the most poorly, sliding 0.88 yuan or 6.6 percent to 12.45 yuan on 661,389 shares.
Blue-chip Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd, which slid 0.05 yuan to 18.87 yuan, registered the heaviest trade of 63 million shares worth 1.17 billion yuan.
Brokers said the day's market was bolstered by widespread bargain hunting and institutional support in key counters.
They said B shares were boosted by a strong performance on the Hong Kong stock market on Thursday.
"Today's market performance was much better than expected but trading should be more volatile due to concerns about stability," a broker with a major Chinese brokerage said.
"It would be tactless for institutions to buy heavily in the coming sessions when the rest of China is mourning," the broker said.
On the B share market, demand for shares of firms expected to post good 1996 results was strong, brokers said.
Building materials maker Shenzhen Fangda Co Ltd was the biggest gainer and rose HK$0.52 or 5.89 percent to HK$9.35 on volume of 2.07 million shares.

Jiangling Motors Corporation Ltd climbed HK$0.18 to HK$3.48 after 1.7 million shares were traded. Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd edged up HK$0.04 to HK$4.30 on the heaviest trade of 3.31 million shares.
